item.description:
CVE-2026-109283 · CVSS 5.4 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:N) · CWE-863
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.11.1, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Revoked users keep signing in via token exchange when roles are only in the ID token
## Summary The OAuth token exchange endpoint lets a user who already has a linked OAuth account swap a provider access token for an Open WebUI session. Since 0.11.1 it applies the OAuth role policy, but it only reads roles from the provider's userinfo response, and it only refuses a user when a roles claim is found. With an identity provider that sends roles only in the ID token (Microsoft Entra ID app roles are the common case), token exchange sees no roles and keeps the user's existing role, so a user whose provider role no longer satisfies the policy, and who is correctly refused at browser login, can still get a working session.
## Preconditions - `ENABLE_OAUTH_TOKEN_EXCHANGE=true` (default `false`). - `ENABLE_OAUTH_ROLE_MANAGEMENT=true` (default `false`), with `OAUTH_ALLOWED_ROLES` (default `user,admin`) not containing `*`. - The identity provider puts the roles claim only in the ID token and not in the userinfo response. - The attacker already has an Open WebUI account linked to their provider identity, and can still obtain a valid access token from the provider (their provider account is active, only their role changed).
Deployments with either setting off, or whose provider returns roles in userinfo, are not affected.
## Impact A user the operator meant to lock out through the OAuth role policy keeps signing in through token exchange and keeps the role they held before, together with everything that role can reach. The attacker gains nothing beyond their previous access: an empty roles claim can neither grant admin nor change the role. Exploitation needs the non-default configuration above and a previously provisioned account. Browser SSO login is not affected and refuses the user as intended.
## Fix Fixed in 10d1cfe63, released in 0.11.4. Token exchange now also reads the roles claim from the exchanged token, and when role management is on and no roles claim can be read at all, it refuses the exchange.
## Root cause - Component: the OAuth token exchange endpoint (`POST /api/v1/auths/oauth/{provider}/token/exchange`) and the OAuth role policy it calls. - Affected builds: 0.11.1 through 0.11.3, the releases that added the role policy to token exchange.
The role policy was written for browser login, where the ID token claims are merged into the user data before the policy runs, so "no roles claim" there means the provider genuinely sent none and keeping the current role is the documented behaviour. Token exchange never receives an ID token and builds the user data from userinfo alone, so for providers that only put roles in the ID token the policy always saw an empty claim and fell through to keeping the existing role instead of refusing.
## Proof of concept Reproduced on the 0.11.3 and 0.11.4 PyPI packages with a local OIDC provider that puts `roles` only in the ID token, `ENABLE_OAUTH_TOKEN_EXCHANGE=true`, `ENABLE_OAUTH_ROLE_MANAGEMENT=true` and an `OAUTH_ALLOWED_ROLES` list.
1. Sign in once through SSO while holding an allowed role, so the account is linked. 2. At the provider, change the user's role to one outside the allowed list. 3. Browser SSO login: refused with 403 on both versions. 4. Obtain an access token from the provider and send `POST /api/v1/auths/oauth/{provider}/token/exchange` with `{"token": "<access token>"}`. 5. On 0.11.3 the request returns 200 with a session token that works on `GET /api/v1/auths/`. On 0.11.4 it returns 403.
Control: a user still holding an allowed role is allowed on both versions.
## Credits - `manus-pi`: reported the role policy bypass on token exchange for providers that send roles only in the ID token.

item.title: [MEDIUM] open-webui/open-webui — Tool source code disclosed to read-only users via the tool export endpoint (CVE-2026-109293)
item.description:
CVE-2026-109293 · CVSS 6.5 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N) · CWE-200
Affected: - pip/open-webui >= 0.11.0, < 0.11.4 (patched: 0.11.4)
---
# Tool source code disclosed to read-only users via the tool export endpoint
## Summary A user allowed to export tools received the full Python source of every tool that had merely been shared with them for reading. Since 0.11.0 tool source is writer-only: a read-only recipient can use a shared tool, and the tool's detail view withholds its source from them. The bulk export returned it anyway, because it selected every tool the caller could read.
## Preconditions - Authentication enabled (`WEBUI_AUTH=true`, default) and plugins enabled (`ENABLE_PLUGINS=true`, default). - The attacker is an authenticated non-admin who holds the tool export permission (`workspace.tools_export`, off by default, set with `USER_PERMISSIONS_WORKSPACE_TOOLS_EXPORT` or granted by an admin in default or group permissions). - A tool owned by someone else is shared with a read grant to the attacker, to one of their groups, or to all users.
Deployments that never grant the tool export permission to non-admins, or that share tools only with users who already hold write access, are not affected.
## Impact A non-admin with export rights obtains the server-side source of every tool shared with them read-only, in one request. Tool source commonly embeds API keys, credentials and internal service URLs, so the loss often reaches beyond the code itself. Confidentiality only: the export grants no ability to modify or run tools, and has no integrity or availability impact.
## Fix Fixed in 0.11.4 by #29310. The export now returns only tools the caller owns or holds write access to, the same scope the per-tool export and the model export already used. Upgrading fully resolves the issue with no configuration change.
## Root cause Affected component: `GET /api/v1/tools/export` in `backend/open_webui/routers/tools.py`. Affected setup: releases 0.11.0 through 0.11.3. Tool export has been open to non-admins since 0.6.37, but before 0.11.0 a read-only recipient could already read a shared tool's source in its detail view, so the export disclosed nothing beyond that.
The export response deliberately includes each tool's source, since exporting is how a writer takes a copy of their tools. The handler, however, built its list with the default read scope of the tool query, so every tool shared read-only with the caller was exported with its source. When 0.11.0 made source writer-only on the detail endpoint, the export path was left on the read scope and kept returning it.
## Proof of concept Against a fresh instance, with an admin and a second account `bob` of role `user`:
1. As the admin, enable tool export for users (`POST /api/v1/users/default/permissions` with `workspace.tools_export: true`). 2. As the admin, create a tool whose source contains a marker and share it read-only with bob:
``` POST /api/v1/tools/create {"id": "readtool", "name": "Read Tool", "content": "API_KEY = \"TOOL_SRC_SECRET\"\nclass Tools:\n def hello(self) -> str:\n return 'hi'\n", "meta": {"description": "poc"}, "access_grants": [{"principal_type": "user", "principal_id": "<bob id>", "permission": "read"}]} ```
3. As bob:
``` GET /api/v1/tools/id/readtool -> 200, no content field GET /api/v1/tools/export -> 200, [{"id": "readtool", "content": "API_KEY = \"TOOL_SRC_SECRET\" ...", ...}] ```
On 0.11.4 the same export returns only tools bob owns or can write, and `readtool` is absent, while the admin still exports it.
## Credits - gigioneggiando: reported the source disclosure through the tool export endpoint.

An unauthenticated attacker can make `get_page_template()` page-template resolution include a chosen readable local `.php` file outside the active theme directories. If relevant pre-conditions for both the server environment and the active theme are met, this can lead to RCE.
The pre-conditions are:
* The active child or parent theme contains a top-level directory whose name starts with `page-` (e.g. `page-templates`). The well known `pearcmd.php` PEAR→RCE transition can be used for this when `register_argc_argv` is set to `On`. The official `php` image for Docker is affected, and the default cPanel configuration is affected when PHP prior to 8.5 is in use.

item.description:
CVE-2026-105831 · CVSS 4.3 (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:N/I:L/A:N)
Affected: - composer/espocrm/espocrm <= 10.0.5 (patched: 10.0.6)
---
## Summary
When a Lead Capture public form is submitted, the entire request body is stored in the `LeadCaptureLogRecord.data`. Later, when an administrator view the lead capture log record (by clicking View from the dropdown in a log record), the `data` field's parsed JSON value is rendered not unescaped, allowing certain HTML content to be rendered in the interface.
## Note
JavaScript execution is prevented by the Content Security Policy. While certain HTML elements can be rendered, this capability is also limited.
